Using the Individual Data Visualizer app

Draft Updated 2026-11-11

This is a draft of the user guide for the Individual Data Visualizer (IDV). It can change before the release.

Is something unclear, wrong or missing? Click Flag next to that part of the guide. A short form opens with that part already filled in. Write your comment and send it. Only the IDV team sees your comments, and you do not need an account.

On a computer, the Flag button shows when you move the mouse over a part. For a comment about the whole guide, use this form.

Contents

The Individual Data Visualizer app lets you analyze event and tracker data. You can show individual records in a line list, or aggregated counts and values in a pivot table. Line lists and pivot tables use the same sidebar, layout panel and download menu.Flag

The app is planned to replace the Line Listing app and the Event Reports app. Charts are planned for a later version, and the app will then also replace the Event Visualizer app. For now, DHIS2 still includes the Line Listing and Event Reports apps, so you can use them side by side with this app.Flag

The app needs DHIS2 2.43.3 or later.Flag

Note

You can open line lists that you saved in the Line Listing app, and event reports that you saved in the Event Reports app. You cannot save changes to these older visualizations in place. Use Save as… to save a copy. If you choose Rename… for one of them, the app offers to save it as a new visualization instead.

Flag

View typesFlag

  • Line list: one row for each event, enrollment or tracked entity. Use it to look at individual records.

    Flag

  • Pivot table: aggregated counts or values of events or enrollments, arranged in rows and columns.

    Flag

Choose the view type from the menu at the top left of the layout panel. Line list is under Individual data view. Pivot table is under Aggregated view. The menu also shows Column, Bar, Line and Area, marked Coming soon. You cannot choose these yet. The app remembers the view type that you used last in your browser.Flag

When you change the view type, the app keeps the dimensions in the layout where it can:Flag

  • From a line list to a pivot table, organisation units go to Columns, periods go to Rows and all other dimensions go to Filter.

    Flag

  • From a pivot table to a line list, the dimensions in Rows move to Columns.

    Flag

  • If the new view type cannot use a dimension, the app asks you to confirm before it removes the dimension.

    Flag

Note

In this version, pivot tables are available for event and enrollment data only. To show tracked entity data, use a line list.

Flag

Choose a data sourceFlag

Open the Choose a data source menu at the top of the sidebar. The menu has two sections:Flag

  • Programs: all programs that you can read data from.

    Flag

  • Analyze without a program: all tracked entity types that you can read data from, for a list of tracked entities.

    Flag

If the menu has many data sources, enter text in Filter data sources to find one. Choose Show more to see all items in a section.Flag

After you choose a data source, the sidebar shows its dimensions in cards:Flag

  • Event program (without registration): a card with the program's data elements, and a Program indicators card.

    Flag

  • Tracker program: a registration card with the attributes of the tracked entity type and the program (for example, Person registration), an Enrollment data card, an Event data card with one section for each program stage, and a Program indicators card.

    Flag

  • Tracked entity type: a registration card with the attributes of the tracked entity type.

    Flag

Two cards show for every data source:Flag

  • Metadata: Last updated on, Last updated by, Created on, Created by and Completed on. These describe the record of each row, not the program: the event in an event list, the enrollment in an enrollment list and the tracked entity in a tracked entity list. For example, Created on in an enrollment list is when the enrollment was created. For a record that was captured offline, it is when the record was created on the device. A tracked entity list cannot use Completed on.

    Flag

  • Other: organisation unit group sets. A group set sorts organisation units into groups, for example by facility type or by ownership. Add a group set to the layout to show which group the organisation unit of each record belongs to.

    Flag

If a program has custom labels, the app uses them everywhere: in the card titles, the dimension names, the buttons and the titles. For example, a program can call its events "Visits" or its organisation unit "Health facility". You set custom labels for a program in the Metadata Management app.Flag

To find a dimension, enter text in Search, or use Filter to show one type of dimension only: Org units, Periods, Statuses, Data elements, Program attributes, Program indicators, Categories or Category option group sets. To clear the filter, click the cross next to it. To open or close all cards at the same time, click Expand all cards or Collapse all cards next to Search.Flag

Add dimensions to the layoutFlag

A line list layout has Columns and Filter. A pivot table layout has Columns, Rows, Filter and Value.Flag

  • Columns: in a line list, each dimension is a column of the table. In a pivot table, the values of each dimension are the column headings.

    Flag

  • Rows: in a pivot table, the values of each dimension are the row headings.

    Flag

  • Filter: the dimension limits the data, without showing as a column or a row. The values that you filter by show under the title.

    Flag

  • Value: in a pivot table, what each cell shows. See Show a value instead of a count.

    Flag

A filter on a dimension in Columns or Rows also limits the data. For example, a line list with Age in years greater than 5 in Columns shows only the records where the age is greater than 5.Flag

You can add a dimension to the layout in three ways:Flag

  • Hold the pointer over the dimension in the sidebar and click the plus icon. The dimension goes to Columns.

    Flag

  • Drag the dimension from the sidebar to an area of the layout.

    Flag

  • Click the dimension to open its dialog. Click Add to Columns, or click the arrow next to it and choose another area.

    Flag

Each dimension in the layout has a menu (⋯). Use it to move the dimension to another area or to remove it. To remove a dimension, you can also drag it out of the layout panel.Flag

Filter a data itemFlag

In a data item's dialog, choose Show all values or Filter. The filter depends on the type of the data item:Flag

  • Numeric: comparisons such as equal to (=), greater than (>) and less than (<)**, and **is empty / null** or **is not empty / not null**. Choose **Add filter** to add more conditions. A record must match all the conditions. For example, **greater than (>) 5 and less than (<) 10 keep the values between 5 and 10.

    Flag

  • Option set: choose the options to include. The list also has No value, for records where the data item is empty.

    Flag

In a line list, if the program stage is repeatable, the dialog for a data element has two tabs: Data and Repeated events. Pivot tables do not have this tab. On the Repeated events tab, you set how many of the most recent and the oldest events of that stage to include.Flag

In an enrollment list, each repetition is its own column, for example (most recent -1).Flag

Group values by legendFlag

A numeric data item that has legend sets assigned can be grouped by legend. Its dialog then has a Grouping section, with one card for each legend set and a No grouping card. With a legend set chosen, the table shows the name of the legend item that each value falls in, for example 20 - 40, instead of the value itself.Flag

  • In a pivot table, the first legend set is chosen when you add the data item.

    Flag

  • In a line list, No grouping is chosen when you add the data item.

    Flag

When a grouping is chosen, the Filtering section filters by group: choose Show all groups or Filter. With Filter, move the groups that you want to keep to Selected groups. If you change the grouping, the app removes the filter.Flag

Organisation units, periods and statusFlag

Organisation unit, date and status dimensions show in the registration, enrollment and event cards, together with the other dimensions of the program.Flag

Organisation unit: choose organisation units in the tree, or choose levels or groups. You can also choose User organisation unit, User sub-units or User sub-x2-units. These use the data capture organisation units of the person who views the visualization, so different users see data for their own organisation units.Flag

When you open an organisation unit dimension that is not in the layout, the User organisation unit checkbox is already selected.Flag

If you choose a level, the visualization uses all organisation units at that level within the organisation units that you chose. For example, Sierra Leone and the District level give every district in Sierra Leone, but no row or column for Sierra Leone itself. A group works the same way: the visualization uses the organisation units of the group within the organisation units that you chose.Flag

In a tracker program, the registration card also has Registration org. unit: the organisation unit where the tracked entity was registered. You can use it in event, enrollment and tracked entity lists, and in pivot tables to count events or enrollments.Flag

Dates (for example, the report date or the enrollment date): choose Choose from presets to choose relative or fixed periods, or Define start - end dates to enter a date range. When you open a date dimension that is not in the layout, the default relative period for analysis is already selected. This is a system setting, and it is Last 12 months unless your administrator changed it.Flag

A relative period, for example Last 3 months, moves with the date on which you open the visualization. A saved visualization with a relative period always shows recent data. A fixed period, for example January 2026, always shows the same data.Flag

Status:Flag

  • Event status:

    • Active: the event has data and is not completed yet.
    • Completed: the event is marked as complete.
    • Scheduled: the event has a scheduled date, but it has not happened yet, so it has no data.
    Flag

  • Enrollment status:

    • Active: the enrollment is open.
    • Completed: the enrollment is marked as complete, for example when the person finished the program.
    • Cancelled: the enrollment ended before it was complete.
    Flag

Create the line list or pivot tableFlag

The buttons at the bottom of the layout panel create the visualization. The button that you click sets what each row is, or what the pivot table counts.Flag

For a line list:Flag

  • Event list: one row for each event.

    Flag

  • Enrollment list: one row for each enrollment.

    Flag

  • Tracked entity list: one row for each tracked entity, for example one row for each person.

    Flag

For a pivot table:Flag

  • Event table: the cells count events, or aggregate a value of the events.

    Flag

  • Enrollment table: the cells count enrollments, or aggregate a value of the enrollments.

    Flag

For more about values, see Show a value instead of a count.Flag

In an enrollment list, a data element of a program stage shows the value from the most recent event of that stage. If that event has no value for the data element, the cell is empty. Scheduled events are not used. To show more events of a repeatable stage, see the Repeated events tab in Filter a data item.Flag

The button labels use the program's own names. For example, in a program where the tracked entity type is "Person", the first button is Create Person list.Flag

After you create a visualization, its button changes to Update, for example Update Event list. The other buttons change to Switch to, for example Switch to Enrollment list. If a button is disabled, hold the pointer over it to see why. Before you add a dimension to the layout, all buttons are disabled.Flag

For example, with data elements from two program stages in the layout, an event list is not possible, so Switch to Event list is disabled:Flag

Next to the buttons of a line list, a label shows what each row is, for example One row for each Event.Flag

If you change the layout after you create the visualization, the visualization fades and the canvas shows Changes not applied until you click Update.Flag

Above the table, the app shows the title, the subtitle if you added one, and a line that lists the values of the dimensions in Filter. Unless you enter your own title, the app makes one from what the visualization shows, for example Events for an event list or Enrollments for an enrollment list. To change the title, see Style.Flag

Pivot tablesFlag

By default, each cell of a pivot table shows a count of events or enrollments. The Value area shows Count.Flag

Show a value instead of a countFlag

To show the value of a numeric data item in each cell instead of a count, put the data item in Value. You can do this in three ways:Flag

  • Drag the data item to Value.

    Flag

  • In the data item's dialog, click the arrow next to Add to Columns and choose Use as value.

    Flag

  • In the menu of a dimension in the layout, choose Use as value.

    Flag

Only numeric data items can be a value. In Value, click the aggregation type to change how the cells aggregate the value. Use item default uses the data item's own aggregation type. To go back to counts, click Reset to count (arrow icon).Flag

Change the displayFlag

To change the display, click List options for a line list or Table options for a pivot table. The Options dialog opens. The options are different for line lists and pivot tables. Click Update to apply your changes. Hide closes the dialog and keeps your changes without applying them.Flag

DataFlag

For a line list, the Data tab has one option:Flag

  • Skip rounding: show numeric values with all their decimals. By default, the app rounds them, for example 3 289.95 instead of 3 289.9544.

    Flag

For a pivot table, the Data tab has these options:Flag

  • Display

    • Cumulative values: add up the cell values along each row, so that each cell shows the total of itself and the cells before it.
    • Dimension labels: show the names of the dimensions in the layout, for example Gender and Event org. unit, in the table headers.
    • Skip rounding: show numeric values with all their decimals, as for a line list.
    Flag

  • Totals: Column totals, Column sub-totals, Row totals and Row sub-totals add totals at the end of the table, and sub-totals for each group when Columns or Rows has more than one dimension. Totals are not available with Cumulative values.

    Flag

  • Empty data

    • Hide empty rows: do not show rows that have no data.
    • Hide N/A data: do not show the N/A row or column. It counts the records that have no value for a dimension.
    Flag

  • Limit: show only some of the rows. Choose the Sort order (Low to high or High to low) and the number of rows in Top limit. Top limit must be a whole number of 1 or more.

    Flag

StyleFlag

Line lists and pivot tables have the same style options.Flag

  • Title: Auto generated, None or Custom. The auto-generated title describes what the visualization shows:

    • For events or enrollments, it uses the program's own name for them, if the program has one. For example, a program that calls its events "Visits" gets the title Visits. Otherwise the title is Events or Enrollments.
    • For tracked entities, it uses the name of the tracked entity type.
    • When a pivot table shows a value, the title is the data item and its aggregation type, for example MCH Weight (g) · Average.
    • With Custom, enter your own title.
    Flag

  • Subtitle: the app does not make a subtitle. Enter one if you want it.

    Flag

  • Display density: the space around the text in each cell: Comfortable, Normal or Compact.

    Flag

  • Font size: Large, Normal or Small.

    Flag

  • Digit group separator: the character between groups of three digits in large numbers: None, Space or Comma. A new visualization starts with the value of the Default digit group separator to display in analysis modules setting, in the Analytics section of the System Settings app. The option that you choose here overrides that setting for this visualization.

    Flag

  • Display organisation unit hierarchy: show the full path of each organisation unit, for example Sierra Leone / Bo / Baoma / Jembe CHC instead of Jembe CHC.

    Flag

LegendFlag

For a line list, the Legend tab colors cells with a legend. You can:Flag

  • choose if the legend changes the background color or the text color

    Flag

  • use the legend set assigned to each data item in the Metadata Management app, or choose one legend for the whole visualization

    Flag

  • show a legend key

    Flag

Note

Pivot tables do not have a Legend tab in this version.

Flag

View menuFlag

The View menu in the toolbar has these items:Flag

  • Hide layout and Hide dimensions sidebar. Hide both to show the visualization in the full width of the window.

    Flag

  • Resize layout to fit: set the height of the layout panel to fit the dimensions in it. Use it after you change the height of the panel by dragging its bottom edge. To do the same, you can also double-click the bottom edge.

    Flag

  • Reset dimensions sidebar width: set the sidebar back to its default width. To change the width of the sidebar, drag its edge.

    Flag

  • Show interpretations and details: open a panel at the right of the visualization. This item is available for saved visualizations only. The panel has two parts:

    • About this line list: the description, who created the visualization and when, when it was last updated, how many times it was viewed, and who it is shared with. Click Subscribe to get a notification about new interpretations.
    • Interpretations: read and write interpretations. The panel is the same as in the other DHIS2 analytics apps. You can mention other users with @username.
    Flag

Two buttons at the top right of the toolbar also change the view:Flag

  • Expand visualization and hide panels (full screen icon) hides the sidebar, the layout panel and the details panel. Click it again (Show panels) to show the panels that were open before.

    Flag

  • Show details panel opens the interpretations and details panel. Hide details panel closes it.

    Flag

Download dataFlag

Open the Download menu. The download contains all the data of the visualization, not only the rows on the current page.Flag

  • HTML+CSS (.html+css) opens the table as a styled web page in a new browser tab. You can print it or save it from the browser.

    Flag

  • Plain data source downloads the data as JSON, XML, Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) or CSV. Use Microsoft Excel or CSV to work with the data in a spreadsheet, and JSON or XML to use it in another system. For each format, choose the Metadata ID scheme. It sets how the file names data items, organisation units and options:

    • ID: the unique identifier (UID) of each item.
    • Code: the code of each item.
    • Name: the name of each item, which is the easiest to read.
    Flag

Save and share visualizationsFlag

Use the File menu to manage saved visualizations. The items that are available depend on your access to the current visualization.Flag

  • New: start a new visualization.

    Flag

  • Open…: open a saved visualization. You can filter the list by view type.

    Flag

  • Save… or Save: save a new visualization, or save your changes to a saved one. You need edit access to save changes.

    Flag

  • Save as…: save a copy with a new name.

    Flag

  • Rename…: change the name and description. You need edit access.

    Flag

  • Translate…: translate the name and description into other languages. You need edit access.

    Flag

  • Share…: choose which users and user groups can see or edit the visualization.

    Flag

  • Get link…: copy a link that opens the visualization in this app.

    Flag

  • Delete: delete the visualization. You cannot delete a visualization that is on a dashboard.

    Flag

To see or write interpretations, see the View menu in Change the display.Flag

Show a visualization on a dashboardFlag

You can add saved line lists and pivot tables to a dashboard in the Dashboard app. When you edit a dashboard, enter the name of the visualization in Search for items to add to this dashboard. Line lists and pivot tables are under Event visualizations.Flag

On a dashboard:Flag

  • To sort a line list, click the sort icon in a column header. The sorting applies to your view only. It is not saved in the visualization.

    Flag

  • Dashboard filters are not applied to these items. If you set a dashboard filter, the item shows Filters are not applied to Event visualizations. Click Show without filters to see the item.

    Flag
